source_text:
Νοῆσαι δὲ δεῖ τὸν πατέρα τέλειον, ἐν τελείᾳ ὑποστάσει, καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τέλειον ἐν τελείᾳ ὑποστάσει,
2 καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, τέλειον ἐν τελείᾳ ὑποστάσει, παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον. {Μ.} Πῶς ἐγχωρεῖ; Αὐτὸς λέγει· Ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν. {Ο.} Οὐκ εἶπεν· Ἕν εἰμι, ἀλλ' ἕν ἐσμεν, ἵνα τῶν ὑποστάσεων τὸ ἐνυπόστατον γνῶμεν. Ἐκεῖνο δὲ θαυμάζω, ὅτι μέμνησαι τῶν εὐαγγελίων καὶ οὐκ ὀρθοποδεῖς πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν αὐτῶν. {Μ.} Ἐγὼ τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις πείθομαι. {Ο.} ∆εῖξον οὖν, ποῦ γέγραπται ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις, ὅτι· Ἐγώ εἰμι καὶ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα. {Μ.} Ὁ ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ ἑώρακε τὸν πατέρα. {Ο.} Ἀλλὰ τὸν πατέρα· οὐχ ἑαυτὸν φήσας εἶναι πατέρα, ἀλλὰ τοιοῦτον οἷον τὸν πατέρα. {Μ.} Θέλεις γνῶναι, ὅτι ὀρφανοί εἰσιν οἱ μὴ δεχόμενοι τὸν παράκλητον; Ἄκουε τοῦ Κυρίου λέγοντος· Συμφέρει ὑμῖν, ἵνα ἐγὼ ἀπέλθω· ἐὰν μὴ ἀπέλθω, ὁ παράκλητος οὐκ ἐλεύσεται πρὸς ὑμᾶς· ἐὰν δὲ πορευθῶ, πέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς ὑμᾶς· καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐκεῖνος ἐλέγξει τὸν κόσμον περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ περὶ κρίσεως. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα λέγει· Οὐκ ἀφήσω ὑμᾶς ὀρφανούς· ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς. Οἱ τοίνυν μὴ δεξάμενοι τὸν παράκλητον ὀρφανοί εἰσιν. {Ο.} Ἀληθῶς οὐ μόνον ὀρφανοί εἰσιν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄθεοι οἱ μὴ δεξάμενοι τὸν παράκλητον. {Μ.} ∆ιὰ τί οὖν οὐ δέχεσθε αὐτόν; {Ο.} Ἡμεῖς καὶ ἐδεξάμεθα καὶ δεχόμεθα, ὑμεῖς δὲ οὔτε 455 ἔγνωτε οὔτε ἐδέξασθε, ἀλλ' ἠπατήθητε παρὰ Μοντανοῦ, καὶ τοιαύτην ἀπάτην, ἣν οὐκ ἂν ἠπατήθησαν ἄνθρωποι μὴ γενόμενοι σκεύη τοῦ διαβόλου. Πρῶτον γὰρ πείθει ὑμᾶς εἰπεῖν τοὺς ἀποστόλους ὀρφανοὺς καὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν ψεύστην τὸν εἰρηκότα αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἀφήσω ὑμᾶς ὀρφανούς· ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς. {Μ.} Ἡμεῖς γὰρ λέγομεν, ὅτι οὐκ ἦν ὁ Χριστὸς ἐν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις. {Ο.} Ὁ λέγων, ὅτι οὐκ ἦν ἐν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ὁ παράκλητος, ἀλλ' ἐν Μοντανῷ, πάντως οὐδὲ τὸν Χριστὸν δώσει ἐν αὐτοῖς. Οὐδεὶς γὰρ δύναται εἰπεῖν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν, εἰ μὴ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ. Καὶ εὑρέθησαν καθ' ὑμᾶς ὀρφανοὶ καὶ ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ψεύστης, καὶ Μοντανὸς ὁ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος ἱερεὺς ἀληθής. Τί δὲ ταύτης τῆς ἀπάτης ἐστὶν ἀθλιώτερον; {Μ.} Λέγομεν καὶ ἡμεῖς, ὅτι οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἔσχον ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος, ἀλλ' οὐ τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ παρακλήτου εἶχον. {Ο.} Καὶ ὁ λέγων· Ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν Κυρίου κατοπτριζόμεθα, οὐκ εἶχε τὸ πνεῦμα, ἀλλὰ Μοντανὸς ὁ ἱερεὺς τοῦ εἰδώλου; {Μ.} Παῦλος γὰρ οὐκ ἦν διώκτης; {Ο.} Ἀλλὰ σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς γέγονε. {Μ.} Καὶ Μοντανός. {Ο.} Ἀλλ' ἐκ τούτου γινώσκεται ὁ ἀληθὴς προφήτης ἐκ τοῦ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ αὐτὸν λέγειν, καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης ἐν τῷ τὰ ἐναντία αὐτὸν τῷ θεῷ λέγειν. {Μ.} Καὶ πότε Μοντανὸς ἐναντία τῷ θεῷ εἶπεν; {Ο.} Ὅταν μὲν ὁ θεὸς καὶ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν λέγῃ τὸν παράκλητον ἄλλον εἶναι παρ' ἑαυτὸν καὶ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ἀποστέλλειν αὐτὸν ἐπαγγέλλεται, Μοντανὸς δὲ λέγει· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, δῆλον, ὅτι ἐναντία τῷ υἱῷ λέγει καὶ ἔστι ψευδοπροφήτης. {Μ.} Καὶ ἡμεῖς λέγομεν, ὅτι εἶχον οἱ ἀπόστολοι τὸν ἀῤῥαβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος, ἄλλ' οὐ τὸ πλήρωμα. {Ο.} Ὅτι οἱ ἀπόστολοι ναοὶ τοῦ πνεύματος ἦσαν καὶ πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι, ἄκουε Παύλου λέγοντος· Οὐκ οἴδατε, ὅτι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν ἁγίου πνεύματός ἐστιν καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις· Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκί, 456 ἀλλ' ἐν πνεύματι, εἴπερ πνεῦμα θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν. Τοσούτων οὖν μαρτυριῶν οὐσῶν τῶν λεγουσῶν, ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμα ἦν καὶ ἔστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς πιστεύοντας, πῶς σὺ λέγεις μὴ εἶναι ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους; {Μ.} Εἶπον, ὅτι ἀῤῥαβὼν ἦν τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν αὐτοῖς. {Ο.} Αὐτὸ τὸ πνεῦμα ἀῤῥαβών ἐστι τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων ἀγαθῶν, οἷον ἐπαγγελίαν ἔχομεν ἀφθαρσίας. Πόθεν ἡ ἀπόδειξις, ὅτι ἐσόμεθα ἄφθαρτοι ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος, οὗ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν, καὶ οὕτως πᾶσαν ἐπαγγελίαν ἐλπίζομεν πληροῦσθαι ἐκ τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου παρουσίας ὡς εἶναι αὐτὸ ἀῤῥαβῶνα τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων ἀγαθῶν;
thought_title: The Spirit as down payment of promised goods
orientation: The Orthodox Christian is refuting the Montanist's claim that the apostles had only a partial share of the Spirit, not the fullness, by arguing that the Spirit himself is the down payment of all God's promised goods.
pass_a_gloss: But one must understand the Father as perfect, in a perfect person, and the Son as perfect in a perfect person, and the Holy Spirit, perfect in a perfect person, proceeding from the Father. {M.} How is it possible? He himself says: I and the Father are one. {O.} He did not say: I am one, but: we are one, so that we may know the distinct existence of the persons. But I marvel at this, that you remember the gospels and do not walk straight toward their truth. {M.} I am persuaded by the gospels. {O.} Show then, where it is written in the gospels, that: I am both the Father and the Son and the Spirit. {M.} The one who has seen me has seen the Father. {O.} But the Father: not saying that he himself is the Father, but that he is such as the Father. {M.} Do you want to know that those who do not receive the Advocate are orphans? Hear the Lord saying: It is to your advantage that I go away; if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you; and when that one comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment. And after a little he says: I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you. Those therefore who have not received the Advocate are orphans. {O.} Truly not only are they orphans, but also godless are those who have not received the Advocate. {M.} Why then do you not receive him? {O.} We both have received and do receive him, but you neither knew nor received him, but were deceived by Montanus, and with such a deception, which people would not have been deceived by unless they had become vessels of the devil. For first he persuades you to say that the apostles are orphans and the Lord Jesus a liar, the one who said to them: I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you. {M.} For we say that Christ was not in the apostles. {O.} The one who says that the Advocate was not in the apostles, but in Montanus, will certainly not grant that Christ was in them either. For no one can say Jesus is Lord except in the Holy Spirit. And according to you the apostles were found to be orphans and the Lord Jesus Christ a liar, and Montanus the priest of Apollo true. What is more wretched than this deception? {M.} We also say that the apostles had from the Spirit, but they did not have the fullness of the Advocate. {O.} And the one who says: But we all with unveiled face behold as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, did he not have the Spirit, but Montanus the priest of the idol? {M.} For was Paul not a persecutor? {O.} But he became a vessel of election. {M.} And Montanus too. {O.} But from this the true prophet is known, from his speaking the things of God, and the false prophet in his speaking things contrary to God. {M.} And when did Montanus speak things contrary to God? {O.} When God and our Savior says that the Advocate is other than himself and promises to send him to the apostles, but Montanus says: I am the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, it is clear that he speaks things contrary to the Son and is a false prophet. {M.} And we say that the apostles had the down payment of the Spirit, but not the fullness. {O.} That the apostles were temples of the Spirit, and all the saints, hear Paul saying: Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit in you, and in other places: But you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. Since therefore there are so many testimonies saying that the Spirit was and is upon those who believe, how do you say that he is not upon the apostles? {M.} I said that there was a down payment of the Spirit in them. {O.} The Spirit himself is the down payment of the promised goods, just as we have the promise of incorruptibility. From where is the proof that we will be incorruptible, from the Spirit which he gave us, and so we hope that every promise is fulfilled from the presence of the Holy Spirit, so that he himself is the down payment of the promised goods?

choices.why: The glossary requires 'person' for ὑπόστασις, and the phrase describes each divine person as perfect in their distinct personal reality.
This rare term is built on ὑπόστασις and refers to the distinct personal existence of the persons; 'personal reality' preserves the connection to 'person' from the glossary.
The verb ὀρθοποδέω means to walk straight or upright; the metaphor of walking toward truth is preserved literally.
The glossary decided on 'down payment' for ἀῤῥαβών, and it is used consistently throughout this section for the Spirit as pledge of promised goods.
The literal sense of σκεῦος as vessel is kept, and it echoes Paul's 'vessel of election' later in the section, creating a deliberate contrast.
The verb means to look at oneself in a mirror or to behold as in a mirror; the rendering keeps the mirror imagery from 2 Corinthians 3:18.

pass_b_english: The Orthodox Christian said: "We must understand the Father as perfect, in a perfect person, and the Son as perfect, in a perfect person, and the Holy Spirit as perfect, in a perfect person, proceeding from the Father." The Montanist said: "How is that possible? He himself says, 'I and the Father are one' (John 10:30)." The Orthodox Christian said: "He did not say, 'I am one,' but 'we are one,' so that we may know the subsistent character of the persons. But I am amazed that you remember the Gospels and yet do not walk straight toward their truth." The Montanist said: "I am persuaded by the Gospels." The Orthodox Christian said: "Then show me where it is written in the Gospels that 'I am the Father and the Son and the Spirit.'" The Montanist said: "'Whoever has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9)." The Orthodox Christian said: "Yes, the Father. He did not say that he himself is the Father, but that he is such as the Father is." The Montanist said: "Do you want to know that those who do not receive the Advocate are orphans? Listen to the Lord saying: 'It is to your advantage that I go away. If I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment' (John 16:7-8). And a little later he says: 'I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you' (John 14:18). So those who have not received the Advocate are orphans." The Orthodox Christian said: "Truly, those who have not received the Advocate are not only orphans but also godless." The Montanist said: "Why then do you not receive him?" The Orthodox Christian said: "We have received him and we do receive him. But you have neither known him nor received him; rather, you have been deceived by Montanus, and with such a deception as people would not have been deceived by unless they had become vessels of the devil. For first he persuades you to say that the apostles were orphans and that the Lord Jesus was a liar when he said to them: 'I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you' (John 14:18)." The Montanist said: "We say that Christ was not in the apostles." The Orthodox Christian said: "The one who says that the Advocate was not in the apostles but in Montanus will certainly not grant that Christ was in them either. For no one can say 'Jesus is Lord' except in the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:3). And so, according to you, the apostles were orphans and the Lord Jesus Christ was a liar, while Montanus, the priest of Apollo, was truthful. What is more wretched than this deception?" The Montanist said: "We also say that the apostles had something from the Spirit, but they did not have the fullness of the Advocate." The Orthodox Christian said: "And the one who says, 'We all, with unveiled face, behold the glory of the Lord as in a mirror' (2 Corinthians 3:18)—he did not have the Spirit, but Montanus, the priest of the idol, did?" The Montanist said: "Was Paul not a persecutor?" The Orthodox Christian said: "But he became a vessel of election." The Montanist said: "And so did Montanus." The Orthodox Christian said: "But this is how the true prophet is known: he speaks the things of God. And the false prophet is known by speaking things contrary to God." The Montanist said: "And when did Montanus speak things contrary to God?" The Orthodox Christian said: "When our God and Savior says that the Advocate is another besides himself and promises to send him to the apostles, but Montanus says, 'I am the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,' it is clear that he speaks contrary to the Son and is a false prophet." The Montanist said: "We also say that the apostles had the down payment of the Spirit, but not the fullness." The Orthodox Christian said: "That the apostles were temples of the Spirit, and all the saints as well, listen to Paul saying: 'Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit within you?' (1 Corinthians 6:19) And in another place: 'You are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you' (Romans 8:9). Since there are so many testimonies saying that the Spirit was and is upon those who believe, how can you say that he was not upon the apostles?" The Montanist said: "I said that the down payment of the Spirit was in them." The Orthodox Christian said: "The Spirit himself is the down payment of the promised goods. For example, we have the promise of incorruptibility. How is it proved that we will be incorruptible? From the Spirit whom he gave us. And so we hope that every promise will be fulfilled through the presence of the Holy Spirit, so that he himself is the down payment of the promised goods."
